I'm here because I saw the link in v/new. I know nothing about fish.

My son has a betta in a 5 gallon tank that he has had for about a year and a half. He loves this fish and has been very good about feeding it and keeping the tank clean.

We are moving in a few days and could use some tips on how best to transport the fish from our current house to our new house. We are only moving across town, but if the fish dies my son will be devastated. He love it more than the dog.

Thanks for any tips you can provide!

Edit: stupid autocorrect doesn't like the second "t".
What is the best way to move a beta?

First of all welcome to the sub! Secondly, well you need to keep him in the water from the tank. Don't clean the gravel and keep the filter submerged so you dont kill any beneficial bacteria. A sealed hard plastic container is ideal and try to keep a ratio of approx 50:50 of air to water as the fish will need oxygen for the journey. When you get there fill up the tank with conditioned water and add the water he travelled in too. Ideally more tank water if possible than new water. If your worried about the water temp. Then see if you can find a battery powered submersible water heater. Allow him time to settle in the tank and keep the lights off for a day if he is in a tank fitted with a light. After that you should be good to go! Just drive carefully :)

This is p much right. Also don't leave him in the car because he will overheat. If you want to keep the water temp stable, which is much more important short-term, you can put the container in Styrofoam or wrap it in a towel, but since it's just across town, you don't have to. Water has a very high specific heat capacity.

Awesome! Thanks for the advice.
